I pinched her cheek.
*Stretch~~~*
Her cheek felt strangely soft and rubbery.
*Slap!*
Ryuuya: Ow...

That was a commendable attack from my enemy.

Kanna: ...Mmm... Nnn...

Ryuuya: If thats how you want it to be...

*Pinch*

*Flap*
*Flap flap*
*Flap flap flap*
*Bam!*

Kanna: ......

Then she found me.
Kanna: ......
*Flop*
Ryuuya: Dont go back to sleep!

Kanna: ......
*Flop*

Uraha: I have a trick for that.

Uraha smiled mysteriously and reached under Kannas head with both hands.
*Thud!*
There was a dull sound when her head banged against the floor.

Uraha: Yes?

Despite her grumbling, she proceeded to do as she was told to.

Kanna: .......
*Bam!*
Something hard flew towards me and hit me on the head.
Ryuuya: ~~~!
That hurt.
I rubbed my forehead and looked down. It was Kannas pillow.
Ryuuya: That one just hit me with its pointy edge!
Kanna: Get out, you fool!
After checking that there was no one in the vicinity, we walked out into the rain.
I ran towards the wall in small steps so as not to make a sound.
Kanna and Uraha mimicked my movement and followed.
I was glad that none of them complained about the rain.
Kanna peered up at the tall wooden fence.
Kanna: How do you plan to get across this?
Ryuuya: I have my own way.
I carefully pressed against a marking I had made there beforehand.
One of the wooden planks fell off with a snap.
Uraha: When did you set this up?
Ryuuya: Quite a long time ago, in case I need to run away.
Kanna: How professional of you.
Ryuuya: Right.
The deep mountain range laid on the other side of the fence.
The thickets as tall as a man were covered in moisture and darkness.
Ryuuya: Kanna, you go first. Be careful of the drop in the ground.
Althought it was only a two feet drop, I was uncertain of the terrain below.
Kanna: This much is nothing. Dont make light of me.
Kanna jumped down without hesitation.
The shrubs rustled and Kanna vanished.
Ryuuya: Uraha, go.
Uraha stood in front of the opening.

Ryuuya: Hurry.
Uraha: Yes.
Uraha jumped to the other side.
After that, I returned the plank to its original position.
Then I climbed the tree a little distance away from the fence.
Taking care not to make any noise, I jumped into the darkness.
I fell into the tall thicket and that hindered my view of vision immediately.
Kanna: You look like a monkey.
Kanna said what she thought.
Ryuuya: Any better way to describe me?

Ryuuya: Why, thank you.
I checked for my sword.
Ryuuya: We wont be seeing roads for a while, so watch your steps.
Kanna: I can easily handle grounds like this... Ah!
*Thud*
She fell down right after saying that.

Uraha: My oh my.

Ryuuya: Keep behind me. Lets go.
We descended a steep slope at first.
I took the lead and parted the wet grass as I walked.
This made the walk slightly easier as we descended the slope.
Kanna was walking right behind me.
Uraha had the tail.
After walking for about one hour...
The ground became an uphill slope.
We had ventured into a mountain different from the one the shrine was on.
When I turned around to check on them, I found that Kanna was slowly falling behind.
Her clothes had gotten heavier now that it was wet.
She was dragging her body along.
Finally, a plateau came into view.
There was some semblance of a path that cut through the wet woods.
It was most likely formed from the footsteps of hunters and woodcutters.
Ryuuya: Its going to be easier to walk now.
I meant that as an encouragement to Kanna, but she did not reply.
Ryuuya: Shall we rest a little?
Kanna: No need for that. Lets continue.
Despite what she said, she looked utterly exhausted.
I looked up at the sky.
Rain was falling continuously on the canopy of the woods.
The darkness was deep, partly due to the fact that we were in ehe mountains.
Just then...
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya.
Uraha called my name quickly.
Uraha: Theres someone else nearby.
I looked around but noticed nothing unusual.
Ryuuya: Its just the sound of the rain. Dont worry...
I sensed something just as I finished talking..
There, beyond the sound of rain falling on leaves...
...were noises of another nature.
Ryuuya: Keep your head low. Dont make a sound.
Kanna: Pursuers?
Ryuuya: Be quiet.
I hastily pressed her head down when she started looking around her.
The three of us hid ourselves and held our breath.
The sound of raindrops boomed louder in the drenched forest.
Finally, they appeared.
I could hear five or six pairs of footsteps descending the pathless slope in an orderly manner.
From the sound of leather rubbing against wood, I could tell that they were wearing armor.
Are they pursuers from the shrine?
That would be too soon, and they were coming from the wrong direction.
The footsteps started to recede a distance away. We were not discovered.
Ryuuya: You can get up now.
Kanna: Hmm. What an inconvenience.
She sounded nonchalant, but her tongue seemed to be quivering.
Ryuuya: You did well in keeping quiet.
Kanna: Its just footsteps. What is there to be afraid of?
Uraha: Theyve descended the mountain.
Uraha heaved a sigh of relief.
Ryuuya: Those soldiers were not from the shrine.
Uraha: How could you tell?
Ryuuya: None of the men under me were capable of marching through a mountain in such an orderly fashion.
If I were not mistaken, they were seasoned veterans.
Running into them head-on would have ended badly for us.
Moreover, there was only one place they could be going.
Uraha: What is going on here?
Ryuuya: Its happening a day earlier than I expected.
Before Uraha inquired further, I stood up.
Ryuuya: Lets go.
Kanna who wasnt carrying anything seemed rejuvenated by her rest and walked ahead of us.
Kanna: Be quick about it, or else Ill leave you behind.
Ryuuya: But thats the way we came from.
Kanna: Y-You cant even tell its a joke?
Her attempt to cover up her mistake was miserable.
Kanna: Its this way, of course. Lets go.

I could not even begin to understand her feelings.
Uraha: Weve come this far.
I had nothing to say to Uraha.
That light grew brighter, like a fire from slash-and-burn agriculture.
An uneasy feeling was building up in my heart.
Uraha had also realized that something was not right.
Uraha: Is that a bonfire?

The fiery ash and smoke it spewed out caused a corner of the mountain to become dark red in color.

Kanna whispered.
Ryuuya: Theyve all escaped, just like us.
That was a lie.
Those soldiers that were descending the mountain just now most likely came to ambush anyone from the shrine who tried to run away.
The only explanation for the careful encirclement was that they were out to eliminate everyone involved.
Everyone at the shrine were sacrificial chess pieces to begin with.
With that line of thought, everything was starting to make sense.

Kanna sounded as if she was trying to convince herself.

Ryuuya: We have to go.
Uraha: Lady Kanna, let us continue.
Kanna was still looking at the shrine.
Uraha: Lady Kanna...

She looked away from the fire and followed me.
After two hours of walking in the mountain...
We heard the sound of water from up ahead which was different from that of the rain.
*Zaaa...*
It was a gully.

But we did not have the option of turning back.
Uraha: What should we do?
Ryuuya: Well have to walk along the river. Lets go.
I started climbing, and the other two followed me without a word.

Ryuuya: Keep it up. The walk will get easier past this point.

The two of them dragged their feet along.
If we kept walking along the edge of the water, sooner or later their stamina would be depleted.
The pursuers would catch up with us in due time.
The bigger question was what would happen after that.
Those who assaulted the shrine must have come for Kannabi no Mikoto.
What did they plan to do to Kanna after they had razed the shrine to the ground?
Bring her under their protection?  Capture her alive?
Or...
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya.

That would work to our benefit.

Ryuuya: You two can just sit here and relax.

If I told Uraha what I planned to do with it, she would definitely refuse to lend it to me.
At last...
The damp wind carried the burning smell of paraffin and resin oil.

I had to let them catch a glimpse of me without getting too close to them.

At this moment, I was glad that Uraha had chosen a vivid color.

Voice: Theres the woman!

Just as planned.

Ryuuya: The soldiers are trained but the chain of command is weak.

Armored troops had no chance of catching even a rabbit in these conditions.

With the coat still over my head, I climbed the slope while watching where I was stepping.
*Wheeee---*
Another whistle sounded.
*Wheeee---*
Another whistle responded further away.
Are Kanna and Uraha still staying put?
That thought crossed my mind for a fleeting moment, but there was no way for me to find out.
Soldier: The woman! Shes over here!
He shouted at the top of his lungs to draw the attention of other soldiers.
Ryuuya: Its about time.
I headed back towards the river.
I rolled down the slope where I came from.
Occasionally I could see the light from the torches of my pursuers over my shoulder.
Before long, I reached the river.
This place was much further downstream than where Kanna and Uraha were.
There was possibly a heavy rain upstream that was causing the torrential flow here.
I threw the coat on the ground.
Then I found a big rock nearby.
I squatted down, picked it up and flung it into the stream.

Ryuuya: The woman fell into the river!

The soldiers up the slope responded within a split second.
Voice: Shes fallen into the river!

I picked up Kannas coat.
Ryuuya: Im sorry, Uraha.
*Shrat...*
I tored up the silky clothes by the sleeves.
After that, I hoisted a strip of cloth the thickness of a belt onto a nearby branch.
Then I threw the rest of the cloth into the river.
This would make it seem as if Kanna had fallen into the river.
After setting everything up, I climbed up the cliff along the river.
I hid behind the shadow of the rock and perked my ears.
Voice: Look! A piece of cloth from her clothes!
Voice: Gather everyone! On the double!
*Wheeeee--- Wheeeee--- Wheeeee---*
They were sounding off the whistles even louder now.
Voice: All of you! Over here!
Voice: Downstream! Search downstream thoroughly!
I smiled when I heard that command.
The river was flooded because of the rain tonight.
And that coat belonged to Kannabi no Mikoto.
With any luck, they would take a few days to figure out that it was a decoy.
Ryuuya: So far so good.
I muttered to myself while trying to catch my breath.
But there was one more thing left to be done.
I stood up and quietly left the place.
I proceeded slowly while sensing for any soldiers nearby.
In time, a few soldiers ran down the slope with their armor rattling noisily.
I hid myself in the undergrowth and let them pass.
Keeping my body low, I headed upstream.
Soon I found a soldier walking towards me.
He was alone and without a torch.
Without making a sound, I took a detour to ambush him.
I stood behind a tree and unsheathed my sword quietly.
Then I kept still.
The soldier had not noticed my presence.
He was ten steps away from me.
Five steps.
The instant he passed by me...
I pressed the blade of my sword against his throat.
Soldier: ......!
Ryuuya: Dont make any noise.
He swallowed.
Ryuuya: Throw away your sword.
Soldier: ......
Ryuuya: Throw away your sword.
I repeated myself again.
The soldier released his black-hilted sword and it felt onto the ground with a thud.
Ryuuya: Answer me truthfully and Ill let you live.
The soldier nodded.
Ryuuya: Why are you after Kannabi no Mikoto?
Soldier: I dont know. Im just following orders.
Ryuuya: What do you plan to do with her?
Soldier: Nothing. We were simply told to capture her.
Ryuuya: Who gave the orders?
Soldier: I dont know.
Ryuuya: Nothing good will come out of lying.
I gripped the handle of my sword and pressed the blade into his skin.
The soldiers soiled face twitched.
Soldier: I-Im telling the truth! We dont know anything.
Soldier: Our leader ordered us to kill the insurgents.

Soldier: Im from Azuma.

I had heard that far to the east of the capital, there existed a mercenary group made up of hardened warriors.

If that were so, then a foot soldier would have no chance of knowing the details.
Ryuuya: All right.

Ryuuya: Dont take it personally.

Ryuuya: Hngh...

*Thud*

Kanna and Uraha was standing there.

Ryuuya: What are you doing here?
Instead of answering, Kanna shot another question at me.

Ryuuya: I hit him with the back of the blade.
Although I used the dull side, it was still like hitting his head with a metal rod.
He would not be waking up any time soon.
The soldiers sword was laying on the ground close to us.
I kicked it down the slope.
Anger, and a sense of worthlessness overwhelmed me.
Why didnt the two of them do as I said?
They were most likely too afraid to stay at one place.
If they were caught while wandering through the mountain...
Then it would have been all over.
Ryuuya: Uraha, why did you move from that place?!
Uraha: Im truly sorry...
Kanna: I ordered Uraha to do it. Dont blame her.
She was quick to defend Uraha.
I noticed that Kanna looked odd.
After Kanna inspected the unconscious soldier, she asked me.
Kanna: Were you planning to take his life?
Ryuuya: Well be in danger if I dont do that.
I could not let the man off now that he knew Kanna had a bodyguard with her.
So it was natural to silence him.
However, Kannas attitude changed after she heard my answer.
Kanna: Have you no shame? You fool!
Even the darkness did little to hide her anger.
I was puzzled.
I saw no reason for her to get angry.
Kanna: Did you not tell this man that youd spare his life?
Ryuuya: So you heard...
Kanna: How could you lie with a straight face?
Kanna: Are you one to break a promise without a second thought?
Ryuuya: That all depends on the situation.
Kanna: Are you telling me that youll break your oath with me when the time is right?
Kanna: Are you one to...
Kanna: ...take a mans life without feeling remorse?
She stared right at me.
Her small lips were trembling.
Kanna: I dont want to be protected by a man such as you.
I finally realized my stupidity.
I hereby swear to follow the orders of Kannabi no Mikoto without fail.
To me, that was an oath that I was willing to stake my life for.
But that might have seemed like a mere promise to Kanna.
Kanna, wet from the rain, glared at me in silence.
Then she said this to me.
Kanna: Heed me.
Kanna: For as long as I am your master, you shall not be permitted to take another life.
I went down on one knee in the mud and placed my sword, sheath and all, on the ground in front of me.
Ryuuya: Your wish is my command.
I lowered my head at Kanna and remained there.
Kanna: Good.
Thus ended our second ritual.
I stood back up.
I strapped my sword to my waist and muttered.
Ryuuya: Do you really believe that we can get away without killing anyone?
I knew I was being stubborn, but the question was still a pressing one.
Uraha: Im sure that youll be able to pull that off easily, Sir Ryuuya.
Ryuuya: Easier said than done.
Kanna: Did you not say that you were certified for your swordsmanship?
Kanna: Now is the time to put your skills to use.
Ryuuya: So Im only allowed to hit them with the back of my sword?
I sighed.
Soldier: Uu...
The soldier groaned.
He was finally coming to.
I took off his armor and binded his hands and legs with ropes.
Then I gagged him for good measure.
Ryuuya: Youll get out of this bind if Lady Luck is with you.
Otherwise he might just die here, and I wouldnt be staying long enough to save him.
Ryuuya: Are you contented now?
Kanna: Yes. You have done well.
She did not seem to understand all the trouble she had caused me.
Uraha crouched down and whispered into the bound soldiers ear.
Uraha: Im sorry for such unfair treatment.
Uraha: But we must hurry on for our own reasons.
Uraha: While I understand your position, well be deeply grateful if youre willing to keep your encounter with us a secret.
Uraha: Will you promise us that?
The soldier was visibly confused.
That was a given.
He would never have imagined to be asked to keep a secret in such a situation.
Seeing that Kanna and Uraha had their eyes on him, he nodded a few times.
Kanna: Good. Your actions are commendable, even for an enemy.
Uraha: I shall pray for your safety.
There was a depression among the trees big enough to hide a man.
I laid the soldier there and covered him up with dead branches.
This way, he would not be seen from far away even if his comrades come looking for him.
Kanna: Can you be quick about it?  What a useless man.
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya, where is Lady Kannas coat?
Ryuuya: Is it just me or did you treat the captive better than you treat me?
Kanna: Did you just say something?
Ryuuya: No, never mind.
The rain stopped and the long night was drawing to a close.
The sound of chirping birds had returned to the forest.
The morning sunlight penetrated the towering branches.
Juvenated by the rain, the trees emitted a refreshing fragrance.
I climbed onto high ground and scanned the surroundings.
Lush green mountains spread out in all directions.
There were no sign of the pursuers.
I descended the slope and returned to the other two.
Ryuuya: We can relax now. I dont see any pursuers.
Uraha: Really?
Ryuuya: Yeah.
Uraha: Weve been very fortunate.
Kanna: Quite so, indeed.
Both of them slumped on the ground relieved.
But that was to be expected.
They had traveled further than their stamina allowed within one night.
Kanna, especially, for she had not spoken a word since daybreak.
Ryuuya: All right. Lets take a break here.
I found a shade in the trees with a good view and sat down on a tree root.
Kanna did the same.
Uraha: Ah, your clothes...
Kanna: Youre still worrying about that?
Kannas clothes were soaked with rain. Her skirt was muddy and ripped in a few places.
Uraha could hardly bear to watch.
Cicadas began to sing from a tree trunk far away.
The weather would become hotter soon.
Kanna: Are you two forgetting something?

Nothing was over yet.
Not until I bring Kanna out of this place.
Not until I lead her to the happiness she so deserves.
I could no longer recognize which way we were going.
The sight of torches and the sound of armor had many a time blocked our path.
Ryuuya: This way!
We changed direction each time, running blindly through the mountain.
Urahas face looked grave.
As someone who was more observant than I was, she might have realized.
We had nowhere to run.
We stopped and sat down at the same time.
There was no hope of escaping.
Uraha: Here, Sir Ryuuya.
She handed me a canister of water, but I waved it away.
Ryuuya: Im fine. Let Kanna drink it...
I was the one most out of breath among the three of us.
The wound on my back was about to start bleeding again.
The one tasked to guard the group had become the burden. Nothing felt more frustrating.
Kanna: Drink, thats an order.
She thrust the canister in my face.
I took it from her and shook it.
Ryuuya: This is all the water we have?
Uraha: Yes.
Ryuuya: Alright. Well share it.
We took turns to drink the little bit of water we had left.
Before long, we were leaning against each other.
The tree was sparse and the view was good.
A cluster of Kouya temples sat on the side of the mountain opposite us.
The hazy moonlight made them resemble paradise.
Uraha: The three of us leaning on each other like this, its as if...
Ryuuya: Were one happy family.
Uraha gave me an incredulous look.
Ryuuya: Why are you looking at me like that?
Ryuuya: Didnt you once said that a real family stick so close together they can hardly breathe?
Uraha: I did, didnt I?
I kept my senses sharp while chatting with Uraha.
The cool night air was mixed with the smell of resin and smoke.
Soon, the army would be all over us.
It was a sudden question.
Kanna spoke out of the blue.
Kanna: Do you have any wishes?
Ryuuya: Wishes?
Ryuuya: Let me see...
I pretended to ponder, but my wish was certain.
Which was to break out of this encirclement, even at the cost of my life.
I must let Kanna leave this place alive...
Uraha: I have one wish.
Uraha: I want to live with the two of you forever.
She was as optimistic as ever.
But I decided not to say that out loud.
Ryuuya: Thats a good idea.
Uraha: We can look for a peaceful land and build a small retreat for ourselves.
Ryuuya: Dont worry about food.
Ryuuya: I can farm rice or hunt animals...
Uraha: We can also become fishermen if we live close to the sea.
Ryuuya: The sea, huh?
Ryuuya: If were living near the sea, the warm sea in the west is a much better spot.
Uraha: That sounds like a lovely place to live in.
Uraha spoke in a dreamlike fashion, as though we were already standing right in front of our new home.
Kanna leaned forward to ask me.
Kanna: What does a sea look like?
Ryuuya: You dont know what a sea is?
Kanna: Ive heard its a pool of water large beyond measure, but Ive never seen one myself.
Ryuuya: Its more like big pool of salt water.
Kanna: Are you making fun of me again?
Uraha: What he said is true.
Ryuuya: Thats not all. The sea is as broad as the sky.
Kanna: Incredible...
Uraha: It contains all the bream and abalone you can ever eat.
Kanna: Are you telling the truth?
Ryuuya: As the one whos going to be fishing, Im not too happy to hear that.
Uraha: We can sit around a fire and grill them with salt.
Kanna: In the winter, we can also eat the snow on the roof.
Ryuuya: You can try, but you may get a tummy ache.
We chattered on, making full use of whatever little time we had remaining.
Footsteps were closing from all sides.
Are they the imperial army?  Kouyas warrior monks?  Or the samurai of Azuma?
I shot Uraha a look.
Telling her to not turn back this time, even if I were to die.
She has to take Kanna out of here.
But Uraha began to talk about lofty dreams again.
Uraha: Those villages by the sea may have summer festivals as well.
Ryuuya: Yes. They have them everywhere.
Uraha: The next time, let us all dance together.
Ryuuya: True. Its boring to just watch.
I slowly put my hand on my sword.
Uraha reached for her dagger in her clothes.
We could not reveal our fear to Kanna.
And so I painted a picture in my mind.
It was a night in summer with a full moon shining high above.
There were the crowd and the festival music.
Flames and laughter were rising to the sky.
Kanna was dancing fervently.
She was so clumsy at it that it hurt to look, so Uraha stepped in to teach her.
I simply laughed and swayed to the music...
Kanna: This is a dream.
Kannas voice brought me back to reality.
She moved away from us and stood upright.
Kanna: My dream...
She stretched out her arms, taking the whole world into her.
It was as if she were trying to take in each and every word that was said here.
Kanna: Not all of the dreams are sad dreams.
Kanna: It has been fun.
Ryuuya: Kanna?
She was behaving strangely.
Kanna: Stay where you are.
Ryuuya: Stay? Hey...
Kanna came close to me just when I stood up.
Kanna: Ive forgotten about my wings after spending time with you.
She undid her clothes and let them fall onto the ground.
A ripple of air enveloped her naked body.
Our lips met.
Her warmth and the shivering in her lips was made known to me.
Kanna: Did I do that right?
She asked Uraha uncertainly.
Uraha: Still a little uncouth...
But she nodded.
I want to live with the two of you forever.
She must have realized it all when she said that.
She knew that Kanna would be leaving us.
Kanna: This is my last command to you.
Kanna: Live on...
Kanna: ...happily...
Kanna: ...until the end...
Her wings spread and burst into light.
The air swirled with Kanna at the center.
A messenger from the sky.
The brilliance was fitting for that name.
Those exquisite wings were a sign of their dominance and superiority.
The wind grew stronger, such that it was hard to keep my eyes open.
It danced, rampaged, and threatened everything that stood in its way.
Even the trees and the earth were groaning in pain.
The soldiers were mercilessly thrown into the air.
The wind had formed a wall completely encircling Uraha and me.
Ryuuya: Kanna!
I could not hear my own shout.
So I could only watch.
Her feet had left the ground; she was rising into the air.
A sudden gust of wind forced the army to run for cover.
Kanna flew low in the sky before them.
She appeared to be displaying the might of her wings to the foolish humans.
And then I realized what she was doing.
Kanna was doing what I had done some time back.
She had decided to use herself as bait to allow us to escape.
Ryuuya: Damn!
I got up to run, but Uraha stood in my path.
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya, you mustnt go after her.
Ryuuya: What?
Uraha: Please understand Lady Kannas wish.
Uraha: She wants you to live on.
Her words put me at a loss.
Ryuuya: But... But Im her guard!
Uraha did not look away from my eyes.
Uraha: Not anymore.
Uraha: To Lady Kanna, youre already...
Uraha looked towards the sky.
A full moon hung in the center.
Kannas silver wings sparkled like jewels in the moonlight.
She slowly ascended.
A chant rumbled from the mountain facing us.
It was a curse of a few hundreds monks, chanting in unison.
They wanted to imprison the demon that was let loose.
The wind dwindled and the light from Kannas wings began to fade.
Yet Kanna continued to flounder like a new-born chick.
The soldiers who were laying prone on the ground got up and readied their bows and arrows.
Voice: Nows the time! Shoot her down!
Voice: You wretched demon!
A rain of arrows ascended towards the sky.
Feathers scattered as Kanna body doubled over in pain.
Voice: I got her!
Voice: Shes hurt! Shoot her! Shoot her down!
Ryuuya: Kanna!
I lost myself and shouted.
Ryuuya: Fly higher! Higher!
Kanna moved higher.
In order to bring our unattainable wishes to the stars.
The curse grew louder, coiling around her like a poisonous snake.
At that moment...
There was a burst of light...
Feathers rained down from the sky.
Kanna stopped moving.
It was as if she were frozen in a void.
The light from her feathers dimmed.
Finally, I could no longer see her.
Kouya was burning.
Hungry flames consumed the rows of temples and towers.
The invading army must have set fire to everything.
Even then, the chanting did not stop.
The monks continued their ritual, even if death were to come to them.
All they wanted was to rid this world of the calamitous winged beings.
My shouts were no longer intelligible.
I could no longer tell what was right and what was wrong.
I had lost the girl I was supposed to protect.
She had meant everything to me.
As I stood dumbfounded in the mountain plains, morning came.
The summer sky unfolded beyond the treetops as it always had.
The sky Kannas mother had yearned for.
The sky that took Kanna.
Unable to bear with the blueness of the sky, I kneeled down.
The cicadas sang their sonorous song.
Kannas words still remained in my mind, fresh as the morning dew.
Ryuuya is a true samurai.
Hes a truly loyal subject.
I punched the ground.
Ryuuya: How can I be called loyal?
Adamant Temple had fallen the previous night.
The sound of clashing swords could still be heard amidst the odor of charred wood.
Small skirmishes were still going on with the remnants.
I stood up and unsheathe my sword.
Im going to charge at the enemy to fulfil my duty as Kannas retainer.
Ill take as many men to the grave with me - these men who killed Kanna.
I did not need a cause anymore.
I was looking for someone to cut me down.
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya...
Uraha who had been silent so far called out to me.
From her voice I knew she had seen through me, and that worsened my sense of guilt.
Ryuuya: This is goodbye.
Ryuuya: Forget about Kanna and me.
Ryuuya: Stay well.
Uraha said nothing.
She blocked my way with an arm.
Ryuuya: Get out of my way, or Ill kill you.
But she refused to back down.
Uraha: Then kill me.
I flipped my sword around and press it against Urahas throat.
This was different from my threat back at the shrine.
I would really cut her throat if she did not stand aside.
Urahas next action was beyond my expectation.
She clasped my blade with both hands.
She held it so tightly her hands were like cloth wrapped over my blade.
If I moved the slightest, her fingers would drop off.
Uraha: Go ahead and kill me.
Ryuuya: Im serious.
Uraha: Im serious as well.
Uraha: Would Kanna be happy to see you go on a killing spree?
Ryuuya: Kanna is not in this world anymore.
Uraha: But you are still here!
Uraha: You are still alive, just as Lady Kanna wished!
I was indeed still alive.
But all that was left of me was an empty husk waiting to be ripped apart by my remorse of losing Kanna.
Please understand my pain...
I feel too shameful to continue living...
Yet Uraha smiled at me.
Uraha: Its not over yet.
Uraha listened carefully to the cicadas and the rustling leaves.
Uraha: I can still hear Lady Kannas voice.
Uraha: Shes crying.
Uraha: Faint as her voice is, I can still hear her.
Ryuuya: Uraha...
I thought she had lost her mind.
But there was light in her eyes.
The light from the last of Kannas feathers still remained in her eyes.
My anger receded.
Ryuuya: You dont know when to give up, dont you?
Uraha: My oh my, Sir Ryuuya.
Uraha: Women dont give up that easily.
Ryuuya: If you say so.
Ryuuya: But I cant keep my sword if you dont let go.
Uraha: I wont.
She held on to my sword with a composed expression.
Uraha: Make a vow to me.
Uraha: Promise that you wont throw away your life hastily.
Uraha: Live for Lady Kannas sake until your last breath.
I could not be sure who was threatening who now.
However, I knew that I lost to her.
Ryuuya: I understand.
Ryuuya: My life is yours.
The moment I sheathed my sword, Urahas eyes welled up with tears.
Uraha: Thank you.. so much...
She smiled as tears streamed down her cheeks.
This was my first time seeing Uraha become emotional.
Ryuuya: Why are you crying?
Uraha: Because Im so happy...
Uraha: I feel the same as Lady Kanna...
Uraha: I cant go on without you...
Ryuuya: You exaggerate.
Uraha: Call it an exaggeration if you will...
Ryuuya: Uraha.
Uraha: Yes...
Ryuuya: Lets go.
Uraha: Yes. Ill follow you.
After that...
We left Mt. Kouya.
My wound showed no sign of healing, so I had to lean on Urahas shoulder throughout our escape.
People whispered about what happened that night.
A winged demon had descended upon Mt. Kouya and burned the monastery to the ground with lightning.
The imperial army tried to exterminate the demon, but they were unable to stand up to it.
A reputed Onmyodo priest used Houjutsu to drive the demon back into the sky.
Nobody knew where the demon with wings had disappeared to.
Half a year passed.
We were at the capital.
Pretending to be a peddler couple, we searched for clues as to what happened that night.
Uraha was the one in charge of gathering the rumors.
With that, we got to the bottom of the matter.
It all began with a power struggle within the Imperial Court.
The band of imperial Onmyoudo priests had colluded with the Fujike in an attempt to gain full political power.
The winged being that Emperor Kazan worshipped became a hindrance to their ends.
However, the band of mercenaries from the east that they hired to do their bidding wanted the winged beings power for themselves.
None of that mattered to me anymore.
Kannas whereabout was still a mystery. Our efforts had been fruitless.
Uraha still heard Kannas voice from time to time.
That was my only motivation for living.
Finally, a year passed.
A trivial rumor in the capital sent us on a journey once more.
In the west, there was a band of Houjutsu practitioners rivaling the ones from Mt. Kouya and the imperial Onmyoudo priests.
If it is possible to seal away a winged being with Houjutsu, will it not be possible to break the seal with Houjutsu as well?
We left the capital and headed west.
My body had stopped listening to me, and I was forced to use a walking stick.
With a disabled body, I became a burden to Uraha.
However, Uraha did not so much as utter a word of complaint.
It happened when we were walking down a perilous path along the sea.
We were stopped by what looked to be a wandering monk.
Monk: You are Ryuuya-dono, the attendant of Kannabi no Mikoto, I presume?
It had been ages since I heard my Kannas name and mine as well.
Ryuuya: Your name is?
When I asked him with suspicion, the monk told me in a low voice.
Monk: He is waiting for you.
Ryuuya: Who is he?
The monk did not reply. He simply urged me to follow him.
We came to a run-down temple deep in the mountains.
As we crossed the dilapidated temple gate, Uraha seemed to be checking on her surroundings.
Uraha: Theres a barrier here...
Monk: So you can tell.
Monk: This is a temple hidden from prying eyes. Uninvited guests cannot see the road leading here.
We were allowed into the main temple building while still clad in our traveling garbs.
In the center of the empty guest room, a small old man was sitting still like a stone buddha.
His black priest clothes indicated that he was the abbot of this temple.
Monk: Ive brought him here.
Old monk: Good work, Ryouei.
After bowing once, our guide left the main temple building.
The old monk slowly turned to face us.
I swallowed my breath.
His eyes were devoid of pupils, as though they had been gouged out.
Old monk: My name is Chitoku.
His voice traveled well, such that it seemed to be coming from the room itself.
We told him our names.
Master Chitoku appeared to be interested in Uraha.
Chitoku: You are Uraha?
Chitoku: To think you are able to sense Kouyas barrier by yourself...
Ryuuya: You know us?
Chitoku: I have heard almost all there is to hear concerning Kannabi no Mikoto.
Uraha: Do you know where Lady Kanna is now?
Uraha moved closer to him, but the priest shook his head slowly.
Chitoku: She is no longer in this world...
Kanna was no longer in this world.
There was a side of me that still refused to accept this truth.
Uraha also listened to the priest without saying anything.
Chitoku: By the way, have you met Lady Yaobikuni?
I recalled that name.
The monks of Kouya called Kannas mother Yaobikunni.
So I told him of what happened.
She was shot with arrows on the way down the mountain, and we had watched her breathe her last...
Chitoku: So she is gone, is she...
Chitoku: The monks of Kouya believed her to be immortal...
Chitoku: She was forcibly kept alive by Kouyas secret sealing magic, and yet they called that immortality...
Chitoku: Pure foolishness, I say.
Master Chitoku talked of Kannas mother as though they were old acquaintances.
Chitoku: Lady Bikuni must have lamented her fate for being afflicted such a strong curse...
Uraha: A curse...?
Chitoku: The winged beings has untainted souls to begin with.
Chitoku: As time passed, people began to imprison them as weapons of war.
Chitoku: Although Lady Bikuni did not take lives because she wished to, the souls of the deceased still gathered around her.
Chitoku: The curse will leave a human being if given time, but for a winged being, it remains and builds up.
I recalled what Kannas mother said.
This body is already tainted.
Dont touch my body, and just leave me here.
Ryuuya: What exactly are the winged beings?
It was a question I was dying to ask.
Chitoku: I dont know the details...
Chitoku: However, legend has it that the winged beings inherit dreams...
Chitoku: That is also the reason why they are untainted.
The priests answer was cryptic. I could not understand what was being said.
Beings with untainted souls.
Beings that inherit dreams...
Uraha: Master Chitoku, I have a question as well.
Chitoku: What is it?
Uraha: Why do you concern yourself with the winged beings so much?
There was no reply from him.
However, this had to be related to why he summoned us.
Before long, the priest stood up.
Chitoku: I have something to show you.
There was a rough mountain path offshooting the main road.
The priest climbed the steep path with an agility that belied his blindess and age.
I followed him with Urahas help.
The ancient cedar trees stood erect with their treetops spearing the sky.
In time, the song of the cicadas turned into the warbles of the mountain birds.
Chitoku: Were here.
We came to a place where the slope became gentler.
Ryuuya: This place...
There was a cave that bored through a giant rock.
In the center of the moss-covered rock was a sturdy door made from evergreen wood.
It didnt look to be opened for ages.
Uraha: Ah...
Uraha ran over and laid a hand on the door.
Uraha: This has the same feeling as Lady Kannas mother...
Although I could not feel it as clearly as Uraha, I could vaguely make that out.
This place was close to the sky...
Chitoku: This cave is said to house winged beings in the past.
Chitoku: But that was a few hundred years ago.
Ryuuya: Were they imprisoned here?
Chitoku: No.
Chitoku: The winged beings are not demons.
Chitoku: Those that once inhabited this cave were a race known as Skytruth.
Chitoku: Since antiquity they had imparted countless wisdoms unto humans.
Chitoku: One of these is the root of our Houjutsu.
Master Chitoku paused and looked to the sky.
Chitoku: Kannabi no Mikoto was most likely the last of her kind.
Ryuuya: What...
The weight behind his words disoriented me for a second.
Something sounded in the sky.
A black eagle was circling overhead, carving out a piece of the clear blue sky.
Chitoku: The imperial troops must have attacked Mt. Kouya with some other motive besides killing Lady Yaobikuni.
Chitoku: They must have wanted to end the worship of winged beings.
Ryuuya: But why would they do such a thing...
Chitoku: They wished to unify the gods.
Uraha: Unify the gods?
Uraha was speechless.
Chitoku: A ruler of an entire nation has no need for wings to speak with the gods.
Chitoku: In time to come, every book and document will be rewritten.
Chitoku: If need be, they will turn the sky into sea, the birds into fish, and fire into water...
I understood what the priest was trying to say.
The last winged being had disappeared from this world.
This made the imperial court even more afraid that they would live on in legends.
Hence, they planned to erase any traces of the winged beings.
Books would be burned, new ones rewritten, and we would cease to exist on paper.
And someday, there would be nothing left of them.
The winged beings would never have existed.
I realized that I was clenching my fist.
My rage was penting up with nowhere to go.
It was then that Uraha spoke up.
Uraha: That would never come to pass.
Uraha: I can still hear Lady Kannas voice as we speak.
Uraha: Lady Kanna is crying, even now.
Chitoku: That cannot be...
The priests expression changed.
He gazed intently at Uraha with eyes that could not see.
Chitoku: You are able to hear her voice as well?

Uraha: Please, teach me the ways of Houjutsu.
Chitoku: You have a strong foundation, but...

Uraha: Please... Please listen to my plea...
It was an earnest request from the bottom of her heart.
Uraha had no intention of backing off no matter what.
After a long silence, Master Chitoku finally spoke.
Chitoku: Perhaps you are the one...
Chitoku: Very well.
Chitoku: I shall teach you.
After that...
We began living in the temple.
Although we were offered the priests quarters, we refused and went to live in the cave.
In this place we feel closer to Kanna. It filled us with a strange sense of peace.
Uraha trained day and night.
Although summed up with the word Houjutsu, there were various kinds.
The ability to read minds.
The ability to cast illusions.
The ability to move things without touching them.
The ability to heal sickness just by touching people.
The ability to make one forget what he saw or heard.
It was said that Houjutsu was able to even summon the souls of the dead.
According to the monks, Uraha was a talent that only appeared once every hundred years.
Uraha learned all that Master Chitoku taught her.
Even so, Uraha did not become conceited.
She wore male clothes and often helped the monks with menial labor.
The monks took to calling her Mother Uraha.
As for me, I spent my days in the cave.
Even moving my body caused me intense pain.
That was because of the wound I received in Mt. Kouya, but I did not regret anything.
However, to idle my time away felt worse than death.
I asked the itinerant monks to gather all documents and folklores regarding the winged beings.
I read every document to piece the information together.
That was my all-out struggle against those who sought to erase our existence.
In time...
The second summer came around.
Uraha set up an altar with a fire in the center of the stony room.
There was no one around except Uraha and me.
Uraha: Let us begin.
Uraha began to chant.
Her characteristic high-pitched voice bounced off the stone walls.
It was the soul-summoning spell.
It would allow her to attract other souls with her own.
All that Uraha learned in these past two years were for her to master this spell.
Uraha: Ah.. Ku...
Urahas temple was wet with beads of sweat.
She was taking the fragments of wandering souls into her.
There was a danger of her getting possessed if she lost focus even for a second.
Uraha: Uu... Aaaa...
Her moans became louder.
Uraha: No...
Ryuuya: Uraha?
Uraha: NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!
She screamed so loudly, her soul might as well been torn apart.
The fire on the altar died out.
Ryuuya: Uraha!
Ryuuya: Uraha! Are you all right?!
I fumbled to hold her up in the darkness.
She was sweating profusely.
Uraha: Uu...
Uraha stirred and let out a small moan.
She seemed to be back to normal.
Ryuuya: Uraha?
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya... Youre...
Uraha then lost consciousness.
Ryuuya: Are you awake?
A few hours had passed.
Uraha opened her eyes.
Her face looked ashen, even in the darkness.
I wiped the sweat off her forehead with a piece of cloth.
Uraha: Sir Ryuuya...
She called my name, looking relieved.
Then she slowly sat up.
She wanted to tell me something then, but she could not seem to put it into words.
Ryuuya: What did you see?
Uraha: .........
Ryuuya: Did you meet Kanna?
Uraha: Yes...
Ryuuya: Wheres Kanna?
Uraha: Lady Kanna...
Her voice trailed off. She looked upwards.
Uraha: Lady Kanna is still in the sky.
Ryuuya: In the sky?
Uraha: Shes still in pain...
She forced those words out of her pursed lips.
Uraha must have seen what was causing Kannas soul to be trapped in the void.
It must be painful for her to even recall it.
However, I had to question her further.
Ryuuya: Can you show me?
She replied without a moments pause.
Uraha: I cannot.
Her tone of voice did not change.
Yet I could tell that she was lying.
Ryuuya: Its not that you cant. You dont want me to see it.
Uraha: .........
Ryuuya: Will you show me?
Ryuuya: I wont run away anymore, no matter what happens.
Uraha: But...
Ryuuya: I beg of you.
I watched Uraha intently.
Finally, Uraha spoke.
Uraha: Very well.
She breathed out slowly.
The emotion had left her eyes. Only determination remained.
Uraha: Please let your mind be still...
Following her instruction, I removed my mind of all thoughts.
Uraha began to hum an incantation.
That was also a type of Houjutsu.
An image that Uraha imagined appeared in my mind.
It was a strange feeling, like having my mind caressed by fluffy cloth.
It was a day in summer.
A gently sloping mountain path cut through the verdant woods.
When I looked up, the sky appeared to go on forever.
There was a man lying by the roadside.
The sword wound he suffered on his back proved to be lethal to him.
Someone was crying.
She was clinging to the corpse of a man who would never wake with her hair disheveled.
That was Kanna.
Her wings, tattered by the arrows, shimmered like the summer heat.
Kanna: This is an order...
Kanna: Wake up... Wake up!
Kanna: Why arent you moving... Why wont you open your eyes...
Kanna: I wont forgive you...
Kanna: I wont forgive you if you leave me behind...
Kanna: Why... Why did everyone leave me behind...
She shook the corpse.
Its ghostly pale face slumped towards me.
That was my face.
Kanna: Ryuuya... Ryuuya...
Kanna wailed.
Kanna: Ryuuya... Ryuuya...
She called again and again, as though she had gone mad.
Thats not right!
Kanna, Im still alive!
Im here! Right here!
My shouts were drowned out by the cicadas. They could not reach her.
Kanna: Uu... Uwa... Aaahh... Ah...
Kanna was sobbing.
She was crying all by herself.
Ryuuya: Kanna!
My cries echoed throughout the cave.
Uraha looked at me.
Remorse overpowered all the other emotions within her eyes.
